tasks.title: Overview repository: four bounded queries
files: apps/api/src/modules/publishers/infrastructure/publishers.repository.ts (or a new publisher-overview.repository.ts in the same module)
doneWhen: latest: active caller books of publisher, any status/ownership, ORDER BY created_at DESC, id ASC, LIMIT 1; series relation returned only when series.deleted_at IS NULL

no migration or index added

openDecisions.question: Backend shape for the archive quick filter and the two new Advanced booleans
options: A: new single-select enum param `filter` = all|reading|read|to_buy|series (mirrors the URL) + new booleans `hasWantToRead`, `hasQueue`; legacy hasBooksToBuy/hasSeries stay accepted
B: booleans only: add `hasReading`, `hasRead`, `hasWantToRead`, `hasQueue`; quick filter maps to one of hasReading/hasRead/hasBooksToBuy/hasSeries
openDecisions.codeMakesCheaper: B reuses buildLibraryHaving flags (publishers.repository.ts:420-440) with no new type; A adds one enum + a switch.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. The quick filter is single-select; an enum makes 'two quick filters at once' unrepresentable (CLAUDE.md §8.9) and keeps the Advanced booleans a separate dimension, which matches the spec's AND semantics. Cost is one assertNever switch next to geographyCondition.

openDecisions.question: Name/shape of the Publisher-Details switch that excludes publisher identity from Books search
options: A: optional boolean `searchPublisher` (stringbool, default true); Detail sends false
C: implicit — exclude when exactly one `publisher` id is present
openDecisions.codeMakesCheaper: A and B are one optional field in LibraryBooksQuerySchema plus one option in buildBookSearchConditions (book-search.ts:16-36). C needs no contract change.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. Spec requires an explicit, default-preserving switch (03 §28, §37); C would silently change /books when a user filters by one publisher. A boolean is the smallest honest contract; B only pays off if a second context appears.

openDecisions.question: How PublishersModule reuses canonical best-offer logic without importing BooksModule
options: A: import the pure function directly from modules/books/domain/best-offer.ts (no Nest DI, file imports only @app/shared, date-fns and a generated Prisma type)
B: move computeBestOffer to a neutral location (e.g. apps/api/src/core/pricing/) and re-point Books callers
C: re-export from modules/books/index.ts and import that barrel
openDecisions.codeMakesCheaper: A is one import. C creates an ESM import cycle: books.module.ts:12 imports PublishersModule, and books/index.ts:5 re-exports BooksModule. No module deep-imports another module's domain today (grep found none).
openDecisions.recommendation: A. It is a pure function with no DI, so there is no runtime coupling. Reject C because of the cycle. Choose B only if the maintainer wants a clean boundary now (it widens blast radius into Books/Wishlist tests).
openDecisions.specRef: 02 §24, §25; CHANGE-MAP Phase 2 'Do not import BooksModule into PublishersModule'

openDecisions.question: Form and location of the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 reference list
options: A: hand-maintained readonly tuple of the 249 officially assigned codes in packages/shared (e.g. src/countries.ts), exported via the barrel
openDecisions.codeMakesCheaper: Nothing exists (bounded search: no dataset, helper, or CountrySelect in apps/web, apps/api, packages/shared; country today is a free-text Input + /^[A-Z]{2}$/ regex, publishers.ts:57,165-169). Labels already come from Intl.DisplayNames (publisher-format.ts:13). Intl.supportedValuesOf has no 'region' key, so a list must be shipped either way.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. The spec says no external API or table, labels already come from Intl, and a static tuple adds no dependency. B adds a dependency with localized names you do not need.

openDecisions.question: Custom publishers whose stored countryCode passes today's regex but fails the new ISO check (e.g. 'XX')
options: A: edit form sends countryCode only when the field is dirty; CountrySelect shows an unknown stored code as its raw value so rename still saves
B: always send countryCode; the user must pick a valid country before any save
C: data migration nulling invalid codes
openDecisions.codeMakesCheaper: Today the payload always includes countryCode (edit-publisher-dialog.tsx :182-186), so B is the default if nothing changes. C adds a migration the spec says is not expected.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. Stricter validation should not block an unrelated rename. It needs no migration and only touches the payload builder.

openDecisions.question: (Drift) Should a custom-publisher rename also invalidate series caches that now embed publisher names?
options: A: yes: invalidate ['/api/series'] (seriesKeys.root) and ['series'] (series autocomplete key, features/books/api/use-series-search.ts:34) in useUpdatePublisher
B: no: rely on staleTime; series cards and Add Book suggestion show the old name until refetch
openDecisions.codeMakesCheaper: A adds two invalidateQueries lines. Drift commit 681f9841 added SeriesView.dominantPublisher and SeriesDetails.publishers[{id,name,bookCount}] (packages/shared/src/series.ts:206,278), and the book form auto-fills the publisher name from it.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. It costs two lines and fixes a visible stale name, including a stale suggestion hint in Add Book. Delete needs nothing, because only zero-book publishers can be deleted.

openDecisions.question: Precision of topFiveBooksCoveragePercent in the API
options: A: unrounded number (or 2 decimals); FE renders '<1%' for 0<p<1 and Math.round otherwise
B: whole integer + separate flag for '<1%'
openDecisions.codeMakesCheaper: A: one division in SQL/mapper, formatting in the card.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. The '<1%' rule is presentation. An integer from the server would round 0.4% to 0 and lose the case the spec calls out.
